transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-16
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Alice Reed (Redwood AE), Mark Li (Redwood SE), Priya Sharma (Graystone Head of ML), Tom Delgado (Eng Mgr), Erin Park (SRE)
Recording note: auto-transcript, medium quality — some names/acronyms garbled

Summary:
Quick demo of Redwood Optimize console focused on prefetch (prefix/KV) + batching recommendations and an attached cost model for Graystone's trading assistant workload. Covered tradeoffs (latency vs token cost), suggested pilot plan, and security/compliance Qs.

Topics:
- Overview of workload profile and goals (Priya)
- Prefetch vs session cache design patterns
- Batching/concurrency knobs in the console + econ sim
- Pilot scope and data/network constraints
- Security: SOC2, KMS, VPC options

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Alice Reed: hey everybody, thanks for joining, I think we have a full house, uh so the plan is a quick context call then Mark will show the Optimize console and we'll run a couple of sims against Graystone's profile and then time for Qs, is that right Priya?
[00:18] Priya Sharma: yeah that sounds great, thanks Alice. quick background — our trading assistant is real-time Q+A, typical prompt is 120 tokens user prompt with a 250 token model response, we do sessionized conversations for the same user over a day, and cost is becoming a problem esp at peak -- it's mostly p50 latency sensitive, p95 can be a bit higher but we want predictable tails.
[00:42] Mark Li: cool makes sense, that's the sort of profile that benefits from prefix prefetch and session KV — we did some initial numbers on your sample trace you sent last week.
[00:58] Tom Delgado: just to add, we're on MajorCloudAI GPUs for now, considering dedicated infra or Redwood hosted for the start, timeline is Q1 pilot ideally.
[01:15] Erin Park: and security-wise we need SOC2 in place, keys with our KMS, plus VPC peering. we will also need audit logs and token-level tracing for compliance.
[01:28] Alice Reed: totally understood. quick housekeeping, I'm Alice, I'll own the commercial side and next steps; Mark is our SE who will deep dive.

[02:02] Mark Li: ok jumping into the Optimize console — first screen shows your workload horizon, here's the default batching policy (batch size 8, max wait 25ms). with your avg prompt lengths we saw 12% token cost savings with continuous batching alone. but the bigger win is prefix/KV prefetch for the session state.
[02:40] Priya Sharma: can you clarify prefix prefetch? is that like sending the history ahead of time?
[02:49] Mark Li: yeah sorta — sorry the term is a bit overloaded. prefix prefetch in Redwood means we proactively populate kv-cache entries for common prefixes for a user session so the model doesn't recompute earlier tokens. essentially you prewarm KV for the frequent prefixes, which reduces generation compute per request by avoiding token re-eval for the prefix. it's different from full session checkpointing where you rehydrate an entire long history.
[03:10] Tom Delgado: what's the hit on memory for that? our models are 70B quant with fairly big KV footprint per session.
[03:18] Mark Li: good question. memory cost scales with lookback length and number of cached prefixes. in our sim we set a 4-entry prefix table per session and a TTL of 30 minutes — that gave ~40% reduction in per-token compute while only increasing memory by ~8% per active session. those numbers vary — we'll share the sim sheet.
[03:40] Priya Sharma: does it work with quantized kernels? we are running int8 in prod.
[03:46] Mark Li: yes, prefetch and KV works with quantized runtimes. some micro-ops differ, slight perf delta, but the econ model accounts for that by substituting the kernel profiles you pick in the console.

[04:05] Alice Reed: mark if you can run the Graystone profile saved earlier — the one with the trading assistant hourly spikes — let's see the cost sim.
[04:15] Mark Li: sure loading dataset... okay here's the baseline: hosted API on our 70B variant, no prefetch, batch size 1 — cost X per 1M requests, latency p50 ~60ms, p95 ~240ms. now enable continuous batching to size 8 and allow 25ms queueing — cost drops by 12% but p95 tightens slightly at peak.
[04:45] [04:46] Mark Li: now enable prefix prefetch with 4 prefixes/session and TTL 30m — total cost drops 38% relative to baseline, p50 unchanged, p95 improved. note: these sims assume 60% cache hit rate for those hot prefixes during market hours.
[05:09] Priya Sharma: 38% is great. what about cold-start users? we have a lot of one-off queries.
[05:16] Mark Li: we modeled a mixed population: 65% returning sessions, 35% cold. the savings skew with session-stickiness; for your traffic the breakeven was about 20% stickiness, below that the overhead of managing kv entries reduces ROI.

[05:40] Tom Delgado: any dependency on model routing? we sometimes fallback to smaller models in burst mode to keep latency SLOs.
[05:47] Mark Li: Redwood Optimize supports routing policies — you can set cost thresholds and fallback to a cheaper model variant if queueing exceeds X or latency crosses Y. the console shows a live throughput/cost curve and will compute composite cost for hybrid routing.

[06:10] Erin Park: about VPC/private — is prefetch stored on our side or in Redwood managed cache? data residency is huge.
[06:18] Alice Reed: great question — options: hosted-managed KV (data encrypted at rest, keys in Redwood KMS), hosted with customer KMS via key wrapping, or Private deployment where KV resides in your VPC (we provide the control plane). Mark, maybe show the network diagram link?
[06:35] Mark Li: yep sharing the diagram — (link pasted in chat) — for Private the KV nodes are under customer network and Redwood agents orchestrate but don't hold keys. we can do HSM integrations.

[06:55] [07:00] Mark Li: run another sim — this time we tighten p95 target to 150ms and allow prefetch but cap memory increase to 12% — result: cost savings 32% vs baseline, but you need slightly higher burst capacity (one extra GPU pool at peak).
[07:22] Priya Sharma: so tradeoff is adding reserved capacity vs paying per-token with more aggressive caching?
[07:28] Mark Li: exactly — caching reduces per-token compute but increases active memory and sometimes reserved units. the econ model includes the amortized cost of reserved GPUs vs hosted per-token price. you can also set dynamic burst to cover market spikes without a full reserved contract.

[08:05] Priya Sharma: are there any known regressions in output quality from prefetch? our downstream is sensitive to subtle context shifts.
[08:12] Mark Li: generally no, prefetch is just reusing previous KV states so the model sees consistent past tokens. caveat: if you aggressively prune TTL or reuse prefixes across slightly different contexts you might get stale context — we recommend pairing prefetch with lightweight evals (small prompt set) to detect regressions. the Optimize console can run a quick regression check against your eval set.

[08:45] Tom Delgado: you mentioned prefix selection algo — is that automatic? based on frequency or latent similarity?
[08:52] Mark Li: it's hybrid — frequency + vector similarity over recent sessions. you can tune the threshold and also pin prefixes for VIP customers. it's exposed as a policy in the console.

[09:20] Alice Reed: let's dig into pricing scenarios — Mark has a sheet, Alice will walk high-level TCO.
[09:27] Mark Li: baseline hosted cost for your load ~ $7.2k/mo per 100k daily active users (numbers anonymized) with no prefetch. with our recommended prefetch + batch realtime policy you get to about $4.5k/mo for equivalent tail SLAs assuming 60% prefix hit and using continuous batch 8. Dedicated reserved pricing changes that math — we modeled 6-month and 12-month commit options.
[09:55] Priya Sharma: what about integration effort? how long to get a pilot up?
[10:03] Alice Reed: typical pilot is 2–4 weeks to get telemetry and run the benchmark. private or Dedicated adds more time for networking and security sign-off. for a hosted pilot with VPC peering and customer KMS wrapping we usually do 3 weeks.

[10:32] Erin Park: confirm we can require SAML SSO + RBAC and get audit logs at token level?
[10:39] Mark Li: yes SSO + RBAC is standard. token-level traces are captured; we can redact prompts for PII automatically. show the compliance checklist? (link pasted)

[11:00] Priya Sharma: ok two more technicals: 1) KV TTL and cold eviction behavior, 2) how we test race conditions on batch boundaries.
[11:09] Mark Li: TTL configurable per prefix table; evictions are LRU and we surface eviction metrics in the console. for batch boundary races we have a continuity check — the runtime maintains a per-request seq id and we only serve when kv snapshot consistent; rare races are retried. we can share a small tech note.

[11:40] Tom Delgado: what's the expected p50/p95 delta if we switch to a tiny 8B fallback model for non-critical requests? any quick sim?
[11:48] Mark Li: yes — in the routing sim, offloading 30% of requests to an 8B reduces overall cost by another ~15% while p95 for the critical cohort remains under target because they're pinned to the larger model. you'll see composite curves in the console.

[12:10] Alice Reed: circling back to pilot — proposed scope: 3-week hosted pilot, instrument your traffic, run the prefetch/batch sim, run regression checks on your eval set, and produce a TCO for Q1 production plan.
[12:24] Priya Sharma: sounds reasonable. who from your side will run the benchmarks?
[12:29] Alice Reed: Mark will run the bench with help from our infra team; I'll coordinate commercial and legal.

[12:45] Erin Park: minor ask — can you include a network diagram with egress estimates and port requirements? legal will need that.
[12:53] Mark Li: yes will include.

[13:10] [13:12] Mark Li: quick demo note — console has a "what-if" slider for prefix hit rate; slide shows cost curve real time. also there's a scenario export feature to CSV so you can plug numbers into your own finance models.
[13:30] Priya Sharma: great. small callouts: 1) we need clarity on KMS HSM integration, 2) we want a clear SLA for p95 during market hours, 3) legal will ask about audit log retention.
[13:48] Alice Reed: we'll include SLA language in the pilot proposal and note retention options.

[14:05] Tom Delgado: any known interop problems with your runtime and MajorCloudAI custom kernels?
[14:12] Mark Li: on some older CUDA stacks there's kernel mismatch; we usually recommend our pre-validated AMIs or container images, but for hosted we'll run on Redwood-managed infra and can test a small sample on your cloud if needed.

[14:35] Priya Sharma: ok if we do pilot, do you require us to move data? we prefer minimal movement.
[14:41] Alice Reed: minimal — we can do telemetry-only pilot first where you send request/response metadata and we replay in our sandbox. full-end-to-end pilot will need sample requests, but we can pseudonymize; we'll document that.

[15:00] Mark Li: wrapping with a quick checklist on the console features we'll use: prefetch policy, prefix auto-selection, batching policy tuning, routing rules, regression checks, scenario exporter.

[15:20] Priya Sharma: thanks this was helpful. next steps as listed in chat.
[15:28] Alice Reed: recap: we'll send TCO spreadsheet, security docs, schedule benchmark session, and draft pilot SOW. any other asks?
[15:37] Tom Delgado: nope, we're good. looking forward.
[15:42] Erin Park: thanks everyone.
[15:47] Alice Reed: thanks all, we'll follow up by Friday.

End of recording.
